newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA's Grenville says watching Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA's Grenville says watching Wall Street.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Deputy Governor Stephen Grenville said on Friday the RBA and U.S. Fed were watching the U.S. stock market carefully for any signs of a fall that could impact on their respective economies.
Grenville said there was a close link between the U.S. and Australian economies and the U.S. stock market did have a direct impact on the Australian economy.
"The U.S. is the major force in financial markets, so when something happens to the U.S. equity markets or bond market then we get the effect of it here," he said.
Grenville said Fed chairman Alan Greenspan was watching the stockmarket closely in the wake of his December comment that Wall Street was showing signs of "irrational exuberence".

"I think it's been on his mind for some time," Grenville said. "The sort of rise there could be something that could turn around, and of course there could be implications for the economy," Grenville said.
Describing Greenspan as a "wily old fox", Grenville said Greenspan had called the U.S. economy extremely well.
He said the U.S. economy appeared to be growing at around 2.5 percent with low inflation.
Grenville also said the world's three major economies -- Japan, Germany and the United States -- appeared to be converging in terms of their growth rates, "and that gives us some comfort."
He added that current OECD growth forecasts were comforting.
"If those forecasts turn out to be correct, and that seems to be a sensible assumption, then our general international environment should be quite supportive," Grenville said.
